text: dsh-seal-scripts 为 DSH 网页端提供会话回顾与可复用工具脚本管理。插件监听会话压缩事件，将被压缩的内容保存为本地回顾，并按设置将回顾内容带入上下文；需要细节时可通过工具读取回顾。用户还可把成功的命令流程封存为脚本，向 agent 提供脚本目录、创建和运行工具，并在设置页管理会话、回顾、工具与选项。适合希望保留压缩前信息、复用工作流程的 DSH 用户。无需 API 密钥或外部服务；数据保存在 DSH_HOME/session-memory。

dsh-seal-scripts adds session recall and reusable scripts to the DSH web client. It saves compacted conversations as local reviews, can add them to context, and offers tools to retrieve details and create or run saved scripts. No API key or external service is needed.
DSH 压缩上下文后，怎样把之前的对话原文留存下来并在需要时找回？
Can DSH keep useful conversation details after compaction and let an agent retrieve them later?
我想把反复跑通的命令流程保存成工具，让 DSH agent 之后直接复用。
dsh-seal-scripts 的功能「压缩会话回顾」：收到压缩摘要事件后，把被压缩的会话内容整理并保存为回顾文件；设置允许时，这些内容可在后续轮次注入上下文，并由工具读取。
dsh-seal-scripts 的功能「封存和运行工具脚本」：通过工具创建可复用脚本并登记到工具目录，提供工具读取回顾原文、创建脚本和按参数运行脚本；脚本工具可由设置控制是否注册。

dsh-seal-scripts README · dsh-seal-scripts：**简体中文** | [English](./README.en.md)

> 把跑通的脚本封存成工具，把被压缩的对话留成回顾。

[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-seal-scripts)
[](./LICENSE)
[](https://nodejs.org)
[](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh)
[](./package.json)

**脚本固存是本插件的重心。** 一次跑通的命令链，当场固化成可执行工具脚本：落成目录、写进清单、注入系统提示词，下一句话就能重跑——不重新推导命令，不改写脚本，不依赖你复述。

**回顾是底座。** DSH 压缩上下文时，被压掉的原文当场落盘成回顾文件；按自然日衰减后注入上下文，需要细节时模型能按线索把原文读回来。它同时是「跨会话固存脚本」的原料来源。

dsh-seal-scripts README · 目录：- [特性](#sec-features) - [安装](#sec-install) - [快速开始](#sec-quickstart) - [脚本固存](#sec-tools) - [回顾](#sec-reviews) - [配置项](#sec-config) - [设置页](#sec-settings) - [数据位置与备份](#sec-data) - [兼容与降级](#sec-compat) - [已知限制](#sec-limits) - [开发](#sec-dev)

dsh-seal-scripts README · 特性：**脚本固存**

- **一条跑通的链 → 一个工具脚本**：脚本全文、入口、参数、步骤、出处、每文件 sha256 一次写全。
- **进系统提示词**：工具组清单每轮出现在提示词末尾（最多 24 条），模型自己知道有哪些能直接跑。
- **按原状执行**：参数走 argv 数组、不经过 shell；解释器按 run 字段选（bash / node / powershell / cmd）。
- **可核对**：跑前比对清单里的 sha256，脚本被手改过就拒绝，除非显式放行。
- **可搬运**：整组打成 zip（store，不压缩），导入先预览再落地，索引按落地文件重建。

**上下文回顾**

- **压缩即留档**：压缩事件一到就落盘，纯代码、零模型调用，工具调用与参数原样保留。
- **四级衰减**：当天原文 → 次日摘要 → 日记 → 关键词索引；被读中时加一级并锁定。
- **按工作区扩面搜索**：本工作区 → 子级 → 平级 → 上级，外圈要许可才读。
- **补写提醒**：日记或关键词空着时催模型一次写完，写完提醒自动消失。

**工程面**
dsh-seal-scripts README · 特性：- 零运行时依赖，只用 Node 内置模块；中文 / 英文双语。 - 宿主能力缺哪块关哪块，不抛错、不整页崩溃。 - 数据是纯文本：`session-memory/` 拷走即备份。

section: 本地目录：pnpm 会在该 profile 里登记成 link 依赖

text:
dsh-seal-scripts README · 快速开始：1. **打开总闸**：设置 → 工具(脚本)管理 → 选项 → 打开「自动回顾」。默认关闭；不打开就不会产生回顾，跨会话固存也就没有原料。
2. **跑通一套命令**：抓页面、转码、打包、连 SSH——任何你真的跑通、且以后还会再用的东西。
3. **让它封存**：对模型说「将上述流程总结成工具」。
4. **以后直接用**：「跑一下 <id>」；想先看命令就加一句「先看看命令别执行」。

一次典型对话（输出为示意）：

~~~text
你：把刚才这套打包流程存成工具
模型：（调用 session_tool_create_write）已装好工具脚本 dsh-plugin-pack，目录 …/toolSequence/dsh-plugin-pack
     入口 pack.sh，参数 source_dir out_dir，下一轮装配后进入系统提示词。
dsh-seal-scripts README · 快速开始：（新会话） 你：跑一下 dsh-plugin-pack，源码目录是 /sdcard/Download/dsh-seal-scripts-0.4.6 模型：（调用 session_tool_call）exit 0，N 个文件，sha256 与清单一致 ~~~

dsh-seal-scripts README · 为什么不是一个笔记：模型很擅长把方法写成 markdown，写完就不能执行了；也很擅长现场重新拼命令，每次都拼得略有不同。
本插件的产物是**脚本本身**——当初跑通的那几行，逐字节存下来，连参数顺序都固定。

dsh-seal-scripts README · 怎么触发：对模型说这两句之一，它自己会调对应工具：

| 你说 | 它做什么 | 适合 |
|---|---|---|
| 将上述流程总结成工具 | 把刚跑通的步骤固化成脚本 | 同会话内，命令还在上下文里 |
| 将之前会话的流程总结成工具 | 先用 `session_tool_create_read` 翻回顾原文（含每次工具调用的参数与结果），再固化 | 换会话、换机器、翻旧账 |

前提是那套命令真的跑通过。写进去的就是跑通的那一份，不是草稿——装完再改等于把整段上下文重发一次。

dsh-seal-scripts README · 产物长什么样：~~~
$DSH_HOME/session-memory/toolSequence/
    _index.json             名单：id、标题、用途、入口、参数、步骤、每文件 sha256
    <id>/
        toolScript.json     清单：脚本全文、docs、hashes、provenance（来自哪份回顾第几行）
        <脚本>              真正执行的文件（.sh / .js .mjs .cjs / .ps1 / .bat .cmd）
        README.md           安装时按清单自动生成，给人看
        <说明>.md           只读说明：坑、路径、速度基准（不会被执行）
    _runs/                  输出超限时的全量日志
    <id>.bak-<时间戳>/      覆盖安装 / 导入时保留的旧目录
~~~

dsh-seal-scripts README · 模型怎么知道有这个工具：系统提示词末尾会多一段「工具组」：条目最多 24 条，整段（标题 + 引导句 + 条目）上限 1600 字符，每条一行——`id（标题）：用途 ｜ 入口 ｜ 参数`。所以封存之后不需要你提醒它有这个工具。

清单什么时候换新（选项「清单词刷新时刻」）：

| 档位 | 行为 | 代价 |
|---|---|---|
| 新会话开始之前（默认） | 会话第一次装配时取一次，固定到会话结束 | 当前会话装/删工具不生效，提示词不变 |
| 会话内实时刷新 | 每轮现算 | 装/删后那一句缓存未命中一次（整份会话重发） |

改这个档位的那一下，会把所有已记住的会话立刻刷新成此刻现词——所以「当前会话看不到新工具」有明确的解法。
section: 模型怎么知道有这个工具

text:
dsh-seal-scripts README · 三个工具：| 工具 | 作用 | 关键参数 |
|---|---|---|
| `session_tool_create_write` | 封存一条链 | `toolScript{ id, title, purpose, entry, scripts[], docs[], params, steps, timeoutMs }`；`replace` 覆盖 |
| `session_tool_create_read` | 回读回顾原文（含工具调用与结果），只读 | `file` 或 `date`+`nth`；`mode` = outline / raw / block；`cursor`、`chars` 分页；`line`、`span` 展开单条 |
| `session_tool_call` | 按原状执行 | `toolScript`、`step`、`args`、`stdin`、`cwd`、`dryRun`、`calls`、`stopOnError`、`allowDrift`、`timeoutMs`、`maxOutputBytes` |

dsh-seal-scripts README · 三个工具：- 不带参数调用 `session_tool_call`：列全部工具脚本名单。
- `dryRun: true`：只回显参数与 cwd，不执行。
- `calls: []`：最多 20 条顺序执行，逐条报退出码、耗时、stdout、stderr。

dsh-seal-scripts README · 封存时的校验：| 项 | 规则 |
|---|---|
| `id` | 小写字母开头，2–41 位，只允许 `a-z0-9-` |
| 文件名 | 首字符字母数字，不许点开头、不许路径分隔符，最长 61 |
| `run` 与扩展名 | bash→`.sh`；node→`.js/.mjs/.cjs`；ps1→`.ps1`；cmd→`.bat/.cmd` |
| 体积 | 单脚本 ≤ 64 KB；一个工具脚本（脚本+说明）≤ 512 KB |
| `title` / `purpose` | 非空；purpose ≤ 600 字节（它进系统提示词，展示时超 80 字符截断） |
| `entry` / `steps` | 必须是 `scripts` 里的文件；entry 缺省取第一个脚本 |
| `timeoutMs` | 1000–600000，默认 120000 |
| 说明文件 | 必须 `.md`，不许叫 `README.md`，不许重名 |
| 脚本正文 | 不许空；不许出现 `<!--ovr:`（会破坏回顾分区） |
| 同名已存在 | 无 `replace` 直接拒绝，并给出清单 sha256 前 12 位 |
dsh-seal-scripts README · 封存时的校验：`steps` 只声明流水顺序，不会自动串跑；`params` 只声明 argv 顺序，不校验名字。

dsh-seal-scripts README · 执行语义：| 项 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 解释器 | bash→PATH 里的 `bash`；node→当前 `process.execPath`；ps1→Windows 自带 powershell（非 Windows 用 `pwsh`）；cmd→`%ComSpec% /d /c`（非 Windows 退化成 `sh`） |
| argv | 解释器参数 + 脚本绝对路径 + 你的 args，数组传递，不经过 shell |
| cwd | `workspace`（会话工作区）、`toolScript`（脚本目录），或落在两者之内的绝对路径 |
| 环境变量 | 继承 `process.env`，另加 `TOOL_NAME`、`TOOL_SCRIPT`、`TOOL_ROOT`、`DSH_HOME` |
| 超时 | 默认 120 s，上限 600 s；SIGTERM → 2 s → SIGKILL；POSIX 杀进程组，Windows 走 `taskkill /T /F` |
| 输出 | 默认 64 KB、上限 1 MB，stdout 与 stderr 共用额度；超限时全量写进 `_runs/`，返回值给前一段加文件路径 |
| 返回值 | `{ exitCode, signal, timedOut, stdout, stderr, truncated, spill }`，不替调用方判成败 |
| 参数个数 | 实参多于 `params` 声明的数量 → 开跑前失败（会错位）；少传合法 |
| 漂移 | 跑前比对清单 sha256，不一致拒绝；`allowDrift: true` 放行并在结果里标 `drift` |
| 越界 | 只跑工具脚本目录内的文件；清单里没有的脚本名直接拒绝 |

dsh-seal-scripts README · 导入 / 导出：- **导出**：自创工具页 → 导出。打成 `toolSequence.zip`（store，不压缩），直接写进当前会话的工作区目录并回真实路径，不走浏览器下载；超过 24 MB 直接拒绝。 - **导入**：选 zip → 先 `dryRun` 预览「会装哪些 / 会盖哪些 / 跳过哪些」→ 确认才写；同名目录留 `.bak-<时间戳>`。 - 包内的 `_index.json` 不采信，索引按落地文件重建；`_runs`、备份目录、越界路径、非法 id 一律跳过。 - 限制：单文件 ≤ 64 MB、合计 ≤ 128 MB，不支持 zip64 与加密包。
dsh-seal-scripts README · 回顾（上下文记忆）：回顾解决的问题：上下文被压缩之后，前面的细节原本就没了；现在被压掉的那段原文会被留成一份文件，需要时读回来。

dsh-seal-scripts README · 什么时候产生：- 只有**压缩**才产生：DSH 自动压缩时，被压掉的事件当场落盘成一份回顾（摘要 + 原文 + 空的日记分区）。
- 工具调用与参数原样保留、不截断——日志删掉之后，回顾里的这份就是唯一原文。
- 子代理会话不产生；「自动回顾」关着时连检测都不做。
- 会话页的「删除并回顾」也会主动触发：先压缩、等回顾写出来、确认多了一份，才删会话；任一步失败都不删。

dsh-seal-scripts README · 四级深度：| 时间 | 深度 | 模型看到 |
|---|---|---|
| 压缩当天 | 3 | 原对话（工具调用与报错被滤掉） |
| 第 2 天 | 2 | 压缩摘要 |
| 第 3–28 天 | 1 | 日记（模型自己总结的） |
| 第 29 天起 | 0 | 关键词 + 文件名，当索引 |

按本地日历日算，不看小时。你指出模型记错时，它会把原文读回来；只有**本工作区自己那份**被读出去才加一级并锁定（0→1、1→2），锁定后不再衰减。子级、平级、上级的回顾只读、不计深度。

dsh-seal-scripts README · 按工作区扩面搜索：搜索单位是工作区的回顾文件夹，不是文件系统递归。顺序：本工作区自己 → 它的子级（从最深往回收）→ 平级（从最深往回收）→ 上一级 → 上一级的平级 → 它们的第 1、2 层子……外圈只有 `allowOuter` 为真才读，否则只数有几份并说明。

命中粒度：先关键词、再摘要、最后原文，命中哪层就整段返回那层；同一工作区内按层级、命中词数、压缩时刻排序。

dsh-seal-scripts README · 补写提醒：深度降到 1 或 0 时，模型看到的是日记或关键词——这两个是它自己总结后写进去的。哪份还空着就会提醒它补，两个位置可选：

- **在上下文提醒**（默认）：并进回顾正文，同一条消息；写完这段文字变了，整条被替换，催促自动消失。
- **在系统侧提醒**：作为系统提示词末尾的一段。模型的遵守程度不同，按实际情况选。

dsh-seal-scripts README · 注入与预览：- 回顾每轮自动进上下文，多条按时间从旧到新。
- 设置页「回顾」页的预览框与真实注入走同一个装配函数：框里看到的就是这一轮会送进去的文字（选中某条时只看那条）。
- 装配失败（例如回顾太大）不会静默变成「没有回顾」，而是给模型一段诊断：几份、合计多大、最大那份是谁、怎么处理。
dsh-seal-scripts README · 和脚本固存的关系：一句话：回顾是固存的原料库。跨会话、换机器时，模型靠 `session_tool_create_read` 从回顾里翻出当初的命令与参数，再 `session_tool_create_write` 封存。回顾本身的细节不需要你调——打开「自动回顾」，其余用默认值即可。

dsh-seal-scripts README · 配置项：| 字段 | 取值 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `autoReviewEnabled` | bool | `false` | 总闸：关着不建回顾、不注入、不装回顾工具 |
| `injectEnabled` | bool | `true` | 回顾注入与日记提醒的总开关（不管工具组清单） |
| `toolListEnabled` | bool | `true` | 是否注入工具组清单段，并按它装卸三个 `session_tool_*` |
| `toolListRefresh` | `newSession` / `realtime` | `newSession` | 清单段什么时候重算 |
| `fullLoad` | bool | `false` | 深度 3 也保留工具调用与报错（官方警告：会全文回灌） |
| `reminderChannel` | `context` / `system` | `context` | 日记提醒并进正文，还是走系统提示词段 |
| `stopLowering` | bool | `false` | 所有回顾停在记下的深度，不再按天衰减 |
| `loadLevel` | `follow` / 0–3 | `follow` | 载入时强制某一级（只改载入，不改已记深度） |
dsh-seal-scripts README · 配置项：两条联动：自动回顾关着时「回顾注入」读出来一律按关算（存的值不改）；停止降低开启时「载入数值」回退到跟随深度。

dsh-seal-scripts README · 设置页：设置 → **工具(脚本)管理**，四个标签： | 标签 | 内容 | |---|---| | 自创工具 | 工具路径、即将注入的系统提示词原文、清单开关与刷新时刻、导入 / 导出 | | 会话 | 按工作区分组的会话列表（标题、归档徽章），删除 / 删除并回顾（都二次确认） | | 回顾 | 日历区间筛选、回顾列表（深度徽章）、注入预览、删除单条 | | 选项 | 四组：工具固存、回顾注入、回顾内容、回顾深度 |

dsh-seal-scripts README · 数据位置与备份：~~~
$DSH_HOME/session-memory/
    _options.json                 选项
    _locale.json                  语言（中文 / 英文）
    _health.json                  每工作区最近一次成功/失败
    <工作区 key>/
        <时间戳>-<id>.md          回顾正文（唯一真相，纯文本，可读可搜可改）
        <同名>.json               这一份的载入缓存（丢了按文件时间重建）
        _assembly.json.migrated-*  旧版索引迁移遗留（永不自动删）
    toolSequence/                 工具脚本（机器级，所有工作区共用）
~~~
dsh-seal-scripts README · 数据位置与备份：- 工作区 key 与宿主 `sessions/` 目录同一套编码：`/` 折成 `-`，非 ASCII 写成 `~XXXX`。 - 备份 = 整个 `session-memory/` 拷走；迁移 = 放到新机器同一位置，装同一个插件。 - 卸载插件不删数据。

dsh-seal-scripts README · dsh-seal-scripts：**Sealed scripts are the point of this plugin.** A command chain that just worked is sealed on the spot into an executable tool script: a directory, a manifest, one line in the system prompt. Next time it runs with a single sentence — no re-deriving commands, no rewriting the script, no asking you to repeat yourself.

dsh-seal-scripts README · dsh-seal-scripts：**Reviews are the base layer.** When DSH compacts the context, the shadowed transcript is written to disk as a review file, decays by calendar day, and is injected into context; when details matter, the model reads the original back from a clue. Reviews are also the raw material for sealing a workflow from an earlier session.

dsh-seal-scripts README · Features：- **One working chain → one tool script**: full script text, entry, args, steps, provenance and a per-file sha256, written in one go.
- **Present in the system prompt**: the tool list sits at the end of the prompt every turn (up to 24 entries), so the model knows what it can run.
- **Runs as written**: arguments travel as an argv array and never pass through a shell; the interpreter comes from the run field (bash / node / powershell / cmd).
- **Verifiable**: per-file sha256 is compared before running; a hand-edited script is refused unless you explicitly allow it.
- **Portable**: the whole set packs into a store-only zip; import previews before writing and rebuilds the index from the files on disk.

dsh-seal-scripts README · Features：- **Written on compaction**: pure code, no model call; tool calls and their arguments are kept verbatim.
- **Four-level decay**: today original → next-day summary → diary → keyword index; reading it bumps one level and pins it.
- **Cross-workspace search**: this workspace → children → siblings → parents; outer rings need explicit permission.
- **Diary nudges**: while keywords or the diary are still empty the model is asked to finish them in one call; the nudge disappears once they are written.

dsh-seal-scripts README · Features：**Engineering**

- Zero runtime dependencies, Node built-ins only. Chinese and English UI.
- A missing host capability disables that block only — no crash, no blank settings page.
- Plain-text data: copy `session-memory/` and you have a backup.

dsh-seal-scripts README · Quick start：1. **Open the master switch**: Settings → Tool (script) manager → Options → turn on **Auto review**. It is off by default; without it no review is created and cross-session sealing has no raw material.
2. **Run a chain end to end**: scrape a page, transcode, pack, connect over SSH — anything that really worked and that you will need again.
3. **Seal it**: ask the model to turn the steps above into a tool.
4. **Reuse it**: ask it to run `<id>`; add show me the commands first, do not run to preview.

dsh-seal-scripts README · Quick start：A sample session (output is illustrative):

~~~text
You: turn that packaging flow into a tool
Model: (calls session_tool_create_write) installed tool script dsh-plugin-pack at .../toolSequence/dsh-plugin-pack
       entry pack.sh, params source_dir out_dir; it enters the system prompt on the next assembly.

(new session)
You: run dsh-plugin-pack, the source dir is /sdcard/Download/dsh-seal-scripts-0.4.6
Model: (calls session_tool_call) exit 0, N files, sha256 matches the manifest
~~~

dsh-seal-scripts README · Why this is not a note：Models are good at writing markdown about a method, and the note cannot run. They are also good at rebuilding commands on the spot, slightly differently each time. The artifact here is the script itself: the lines that worked, stored byte for byte, argument order included.
section: Why this is not a note

text:
dsh-seal-scripts README · How to trigger it：| What you say | What happens | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| turn the steps above into a tool | seals the steps that just ran | same session, commands still in context |
| turn the workflow from an earlier session into a tool | reads review originals first with `session_tool_create_read` (every tool call and its arguments), then seals | new session, new machine, old history |
dsh-seal-scripts README · How to trigger it：The chain must have worked. What gets stored is the version that ran, not a draft — editing after installing means re-sending the whole context.

dsh-seal-scripts README · What gets created：~~~
$DSH_HOME/session-memory/toolSequence/
    _index.json             registry: id, title, purpose, entry, args, steps, per-file sha256
    <id>/
        toolScript.json     manifest: full script text, docs, hashes, provenance (review file + line)
        <script>            the file that actually runs (.sh / .js .mjs .cjs / .ps1 / .bat .cmd)
        README.md           generated from the manifest at install time, for humans
        <notes>.md          read-only notes: pitfalls, paths, benchmarks (never executed)
    _runs/                  full logs of output that exceeded the cap
    <id>.bak-<timestamp>/   previous directory kept on reinstall or import
~~~

dsh-seal-scripts README · How the model learns about it：The end of the system prompt gains a toolSequence block: at most 24 entries, and the whole block (header + guide + entries) is capped at 1600 characters, one line each — `· id (title): purpose｜entry <entry>｜args <p1> <p2>`. After sealing you never have to remind the model that the tool exists.

When that list refreshes (option **When the list is refreshed**):
section: How the model learns about it

text:
dsh-seal-scripts README · How the model learns about it：| Mode | Behaviour | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Before a new session (default) | computed once at the first assembly, then fixed until the session ends | installing or removing a tool mid-session leaves the prompt unchanged |
| Live per session | computed every turn | one cache miss on the next message (the whole session is resent) |

Changing that mode refreshes every remembered session to the current list — so there is a defined way out of the current session does not see the new tool case.
section: How the model learns about it

text:
dsh-seal-scripts README · The three tools：| Tool | Purpose | Key arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `session_tool_create_write` | seal a chain | `toolScript{ id, title, purpose, entry, scripts[], docs[], params, steps, timeoutMs }`; `replace` overwrites |
| `session_tool_create_read` | read review originals (tool calls and results included), read-only | `file` or `date`+`nth`; `mode` = outline / raw / block; `cursor`, `chars` paging; `line`, `span` for one call |
| `session_tool_call` | run as written | `toolScript`, `step`, `args`, `stdin`, `cwd`, `dryRun`, `calls`, `stopOnError`, `allowDrift`, `timeoutMs`, `maxOutputBytes` |

dsh-seal-scripts README · The three tools：- Calling `session_tool_call` without arguments lists every tool script.
- `dryRun: true` echoes the arguments and cwd without running.
- `calls: []` runs up to 20 entries in order, reporting exit code, duration, stdout and stderr per entry.

dsh-seal-scripts README · Validation when sealing：| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| `id` | starts with a lowercase letter, 2–41 chars, only `a-z0-9-` |
| file name | starts alphanumeric, no leading dot, no path separators, up to 61 chars |
| `run` vs extension | bash→`.sh`; node→`.js/.mjs/.cjs`; ps1→`.ps1`; cmd→`.bat/.cmd` |
| size | one script ≤ 64 KB; one tool script (scripts + docs) ≤ 512 KB |
| `title` / `purpose` | non-empty; purpose ≤ 600 bytes (it enters the prompt; display truncates at 80 chars) |
| `entry` / `steps` | must name files in `scripts`; entry defaults to the first script |
| `timeoutMs` | 1000–600000, default 120000 |
| docs | must be `.md`, may not be called `README.md`, no duplicates |
| script body | non-empty; must not contain `<!--ovr:` (it would break review markers) |
| same id exists | refused without `replace`; the error quotes the first 12 hex chars of the manifest sha256 |
dsh-seal-scripts README · Validation when sealing：`steps` only declares pipeline order and never runs anything by itself; `params` only declares argv order and names are not validated.

dsh-seal-scripts README · Execution semantics：| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| interpreter | bash→`bash` from PATH; node→current `process.execPath`; ps1→Windows PowerShell (or `pwsh` elsewhere); cmd→`%ComSpec% /d /c` (falls back to `sh` off Windows) |
| argv | interpreter arguments + absolute script path + your args, passed as an array, never through a shell |
| cwd | `workspace` (session workspace), `toolScript` (the script directory), or an absolute path inside either |
| environment | inherits `process.env`, plus `TOOL_NAME`, `TOOL_SCRIPT`, `TOOL_ROOT`, `DSH_HOME` |
| timeout | 120 s by default, 600 s maximum; SIGTERM → 2 s → SIGKILL; process group on POSIX, `taskkill /T /F` on Windows |
| output | 64 KB default, 1 MB maximum, stdout and stderr share the budget; overflow goes in full to `_runs/` and the reply carries the head plus the file path |
| result | `{ exitCode, signal, timedOut, stdout, stderr, truncated, spill }`; success is not judged for the caller |
| argument count | more arguments than `params` declares fails before running (they would shift); fewer is fine |
| drift | sha256 is compared first; mismatch refuses, `allowDrift: true` allows it and marks the result |
| co

dsh-seal-scripts README · Import / export：- **Export**: Sealed tools tab → Export. Packs `toolSequence.zip` (store, no compression) straight into the current session workspace and returns the real path — no browser download. Over 24 MB is refused.
- **Import**: pick a zip → `dryRun` preview of what will be installed, overwritten and skipped → confirm to write. An existing directory is kept as `.bak-<timestamp>`.
- `_index.json` inside the package is not trusted; the index is rebuilt from the files on disk. `_runs`, backup directories, escaping paths and invalid ids are skipped.
- Limits: 64 MB per entry, 128 MB total; zip64 and encrypted archives are not supported.

dsh-seal-scripts README · Reviews and context memory：The problem reviews solve: after compaction the earlier detail is normally gone. Now the shadowed transcript is kept as a file and can be read back when it matters.

dsh-seal-scripts README · When a review is created：- Only on **compaction**: when DSH compacts, the shadowed events are written as one review file (summary + original + an empty diary section).
- Tool calls and their arguments are kept verbatim, never truncated — once the log is gone, this copy is the only original.
- Spawned subagent sessions produce nothing; with Auto review off, not even detection happens.
- Delete + review in the Sessions tab triggers one on purpose: compact, wait for the review to land, confirm a new one appeared, and only then delete. Any failed step aborts the deletion.

dsh-seal-scripts README · Four levels：| Day | Level | What the model sees |
|---|---|---|
| the day of compaction | 3 | the original dialogue (tool calls and errors filtered out) |
| day 2 | 2 | the compaction summary |
| days 3–28 | 1 | the diary (written by the model) |
| day 29 and later | 0 | keywords plus the file name, as an index |

dsh-seal-scripts README · Four levels：Days are local calendar days; the hour does not matter. When you point out a misremembered detail, the model reads the original back; only reading the workspace own copy bumps and pins the level (0→1, 1→2), and a pinned review stops decaying. Reviews of child, sibling and parent workspaces are read-only and do not change levels.

dsh-seal-scripts README · Cross-workspace search：The unit is a workspace review folder, not a filesystem walk. Order: this workspace → its children (deepest first) → siblings (deepest first) → the parent → the parent siblings → their level-1, level-2 children, and so on. Outer rings are only read when `allowOuter` is true; otherwise the count is reported.

Granularity: keywords first, then summary, then original; the block that matches is returned whole. Within a workspace, hits sort by level, then matched terms, then compaction time.

dsh-seal-scripts README · Diary nudges：At level 1 or 0 the model sees the diary or the keywords — both written by the model itself. While either is empty it is asked to finish, in one of two places:

- **In context** (default): appended to the review text in the same message; once written the text changes, the message is replaced and the nudge disappears.
- **In the system prompt**: supplied as a trailing prompt section. Compliance differs between the two; pick the one that works for you.

dsh-seal-scripts README · Injection and preview：- Reviews enter the context every turn, oldest first.
- The preview box on the Reviews tab runs the same assembly function as the real injection: what you see is what that turn receives (selecting one review shows only that one).
- If assembly fails (a review too large) it does not silently become no reviews; the model gets a diagnostic: how many, total size, the largest file, what to do.

dsh-seal-scripts README · How it relates to sealing：In one line: reviews are the raw-material store for sealing. Across sessions and machines the model uses `session_tool_create_read` to find the original commands and arguments, then `session_tool_create_write` to seal them. You do not need to tune the review side — turn on Auto review and keep the defaults.
dsh-seal-scripts README · Configuration：Stored in `$DSH_HOME/session-memory/_options.json`; changes apply immediately and are shared by all workspaces.

dsh-seal-scripts README · Configuration：| Field | Values | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `autoReviewEnabled` | bool | `false` | master switch: no reviews, no injection, no review tools when off |
| `injectEnabled` | bool | `true` | recall injection and diary nudges (does not cover the tool list) |
| `toolListEnabled` | bool | `true` | inject the toolSequence block and install/remove the three `session_tool_*` tools |
| `toolListRefresh` | `newSession` / `realtime` | `newSession` | when the list is recomputed |
| `fullLoad` | bool | `false` | keep tool calls and errors at level 3 (warned: full re-injection after every compaction) |
| `reminderChannel` | `context` / `system` | `context` | diary nudge inside the review text or as a prompt section |
| `stopLowering` | bool | `false` | every review keeps its recorded level; no daily decay |
| `loadLevel` | `follow` / 0–3 | `follow` | force a level at load time (does not change the recorded depth) |

dsh-seal-scripts README · Configuration：Two couplings: with Auto review off, the effective `injectEnabled` is always false (the stored value is untouched); with Stop lowering on, Load level falls back to follow.

dsh-seal-scripts README · Settings page：| Tab | Contents |
|---|---|
| Sealed tools (shown as `toolList` in the English UI) | tool path, the prompt text about to be injected, "Inject toolSequence list" toggle and refresh mode, import / export |
| Sessions | sessions grouped by workspace (title, archived badge), Delete / Delete + review, both confirmed |
| Reviews | calendar range filter, review list with depth badges, injection preview, delete one review |
| Options | four groups: Sealed tools, Recall injection, Review content, Review depth |

dsh-seal-scripts README · Data and backup：~~~
$DSH_HOME/session-memory/
    _options.json                 options
    _locale.json                  language (zh / en)
    _health.json                  last success/failure per workspace
    <workspace key>/
        <stamp>-<id>.md           review text (the single source of truth, plain text, readable and searchable)
        <same name>.json          load cache for that review (rebuilt from file time if lost)
        _assembly.json.migrated-*  leftover of the old single-file index (never auto-deleted)
    toolSequence/                 tool scripts (machine level, shared by all workspaces)
~~~

dsh-seal-scripts README · Data and backup：- The workspace key uses the same encoding as the host `sessions/` folders: `/` becomes `-`, non-ASCII becomes `~XXXX`.
- Backup: copy the whole `session-memory/`. Migration: put it at the same place on the new machine and install the same plugin.
- Uninstalling the plugin deletes no data.
dsh-seal-scripts README · Compatibility and degradation：Missing host capabilities disable the matching block; everything else keeps working (the settings page lists what is missing):

dsh-seal-scripts README · Compatibility and degradation：| Missing | Effect |
|---|---|
| `systemPrompt.context` | recall injection off |
| `systemPrompt.section` | diary nudge section and toolSequence block do not appear |
| `tools.register` | none of the five tools is installed |
| `webServer.register` | the settings endpoints are not installed |
| `agents.create` / `resume` | only Delete live session / Delete + review are off |

dsh-seal-scripts README · Compatibility and degradation：Session logs are multi-frame zstd and are split by frame header before decoding; when `zlib.zstdDecompressSync` is absent the built-in decoder takes over, so Node 18 still reads titles.

dsh-seal-scripts README · Known limitations：- Tool scripts have **no delete or edit in the UI**: delete by reinstalling (a `.bak-` is kept) or by removing the directory — the registry keeps the entry and later runs report that the directory is missing.
- `steps` do not chain automatically; use `calls` for a sequence.
- Reviews are created on compaction only; the Reviews tab has a calendar filter and no full-text search.
- Subagent sessions produce no reviews and no diary nudges.
- Import and export cover tool scripts only, not reviews; copy `session-memory/` for those.
